title: Refine weekly cut + RC protocol with LTS gating and automated release notes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Standardize the weekly release-cut procedure and RC promotion semantics to support both fast cadence weekly builds and a separate LTS channel with explicit gating. We want deterministic RC tags, machine-generated release notes, and a set of automated rollout gates (tests, SLO canaries, security scans) that reduce manual toil and incidents.

Background: We've been running weekly builds with ad-hoc tagging and manual release notes, which causes variability and slow LTS cut decisions. This ticket consolidates the cut window, formalizes RC naming, implements release-notes generation from PR metadata, and adds gating checks into the cut pipeline. LTS cuts require an additional sign-off and stricter regression tolerances.

Success criteria:
- A documented weekly cut window and automated GH Action that performs the cut job (branch create, RC tag, release notes draft).
- RC tag format is deterministic: v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}-rc{N} and promotion rules are defined.
- Release notes are auto-generated from merged PRs since last tag, grouped by label (breaking, feature, fix), and published as a draft on GitHub.
- Gating checks run automatically: unit/integration/e2e, SAST license scan, and canary SLO checks. Failures block RC publish and notify owners.
- LTS channel cuts require manual PM/ENG approval via Slack/PR review and include an extra full regression run.

Acceptance criteria:
- GH Actions pipeline release/cut exists and is green on test run.
- Generated release notes include changelog, upgrade notes, and links to migration docs.
- Canary promotion policy executed: 10% -> 50% -> 100% rollouts with automatic rollback if error_rate > 0.5% or p95 latency regresses by >15%.
- Runbook updated at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RN/Release+Playbook and linked from the cut job.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Define cut schedule: Thursday 03:00 UTC weekly; emergency hotfix path outside schedule.
2) Implement GH Action (release-scripts) to: create release branch release/{minor}.{patch}, run pre-cut checks, run unit/integration smoke, tag vX.Y.Z-rcN, generate release notes, create GitHub Release draft.
3) Wire gating: integrate SLO canary job (canary-evaluator) that reads telemetry from staging and run thresholds. Block promotion if thresholds exceeded.
4) LTS process: mark releases with label `lts-candidate`; require `LTS-APPROVED` review and full regression suite; output LTS channel tag format x.y-lts-vN.
5) Rollout orchestration: reuse `rw-rollout` CLI to execute traffic shifting and step-based rollouts, capture metrics to dashboard.
6) Add automated changelog/notes using merged PR metadata (labels, breaking-change footnotes) and append upgrade instructions for consumers.

Notes about trade-offs:
- We prioritize automated checks to reduce human error but accept that some LTS decisions remain manual due to customer commitments.
- Canary thresholds are conservative initially; we will tune after two cycles using historical telemetry.
- Generating release notes from PRs mandates consistent PR labeling; we will onboard teams with a PR template and a lightweight pre-merge labeler bot.
acceptance_criteria: GH Action release/cut pipeline added to release-scripts and passing in CI
